CHAPTER I
GENERAL DESCRIPTION OF THE PROJECT
A. Type of Action
The Randolph Urban Renewal Area, Project Number Va. R-58, a Title I project, is located in Richmond, Virginia (See Figure No. 1). Title I of the Housing Act of 1949 (Public Law 81-171), as amended, authorizes Federal Assistance in the elimination of slum conditions and prevention of the spread of urban blight. HUD funding is allocated in the form of grants, planning advances, and temporary loans to finance area renewal through survey and planning, land acquisition and clearance, new building construction, and upgrading of publicly owned infrastructure facilities. Relocation payments are given to any individual, family, or business displaced by project action Federal rehabilitation grants and loans are available to eligible owners and tenants of property in the area.
B. Project Area
The Randolph Urban Renewal Area is predominantly residential in character. Ninety-six percent (96%) of the project's 380 acres exclusive of streets, alleys, and public right-of-ways, are residential. This residential area contains 2,172 properties and 2,290 principal structures. Eighty percent (80%) of these, or 1,833 principal structures are in dilapidated, deteriorated or deteriorating condition and require clearance or rehabilitation. Seventy-six and five-tenths percent (76.5%) of all property within the area is in a dilapidated, deteriorated, or deteriorating condition or suffers from a severe environmental deficiency.
The Randolph Community is bordered on the north by the alley between Cary Street and Parkwood Avenue adjacent to the Downtown Expressway right-of-way. The eastern border is defined by Linden Street and Hollywood Cemetery, and the southern border consists of Riverview Cemetary, Colorado Avenue, and the Maymount Community. Byrd Park and Davis Avenue adjacent to Byrd Park establish the western boundary (See Figure No. 2).
The northern boundary of the Randolph Community is adjacent to an area cleared several years ago by the Richmond Metropolitan Authority. This swath of land will be developed as the site of the proposed Downtown Expressway right-of-way. At the present time, however, the strip remains unimproved and construction there is expected to begin in 1973.
